appraisal_events.evidence: un accent volontairement tendre qui contrastait tant avec sa tendresse spontanée d'autrefois...ce qui était le plus déplaisant dans tout cela était encore l'amour-propre, car Saint-Loup était flatté d'être aimé par Gilberte, et...donnait...des détails qu'il savait bien exagérés sinon inventés de toute pièce, lui à qui Morel demandait chaque jour plus d'argent.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes Saint-Loup's tenderness toward Gilberte as theatrical and his account of being loved by Morel as vain self-deception, even as Morel, whom he really loves, extracts ever more money from him.

appraisal_events.evidence: sa manière de sveltesse hautaine...s'exagérait, se figeait...faisait de lui une espèce si rare, si précieuse, qu'on aurait voulu la posséder pour une collection ornithologique...des mouvements de cou tellement plus souples, plus fiers et plus coquets que n'en ont les humains.
appraisal_events.explanation: Glimpsed later at a party, Saint-Loup's once-natural aristocratic bearing has calcified into an exaggerated performance; the narrator's admiration is inseparable from an objectifying, 'zoological' framing that reduces him to a rare specimen rather than a man.

appraisal_events.evidence: M. de Courvoisier n'en aima que plus sa femme, redoubla de zèle prolifique et elle et lui étaient cités comme le meilleur ménage de Paris.
appraisal_events.explanation: The Courvoisier marriage is explicitly cited by society as exemplary, set up as the positive counterpart to Saint-Loup's case.

appraisal_events.evidence: On n'en disait point autant de celui de Saint-Loup parce que Robert au lieu de se contenter de l'inversion, faisait mourir sa femme de jalousie en cherchant sans plaisir des maîtresses !
appraisal_events.explanation: Unlike the Courvoisier, Saint-Loup's household is not cited as exemplary: his joyless pursuit of mistresses, rather than mere inversion, drives his wife to despairing jealousy.

status_effects.explanation: Across two separately observed moments, Saint-Loup is shown as vain and self-deceiving, and later as an exaggerated, dehumanized performance of his former self.
In contrast to the Courvoisier, whose marriage is publicly cited as exemplary, Saint-Loup's household carries no such reputation because of his cruel, joyless philandering.
Morel holds financial and emotional leverage over Saint-Loup, extracting ever more money while Saint-Loup exaggerates the depth of Morel's supposed affection.
He and his wife are explicitly cited by society as the best household in Paris.
Her husband's joyless pursuit of mistresses drives her to despairing jealousy, leaving her the suffering, powerless party in the marriage.

ambiguities: In E2, the bird/zoological imagery fuses aesthetic admiration with an objectifying, dehumanizing framing, so its polarity is read as mixed rather than purely positive.
